title: Assessment of the extent of movement (ROM) after two-stage revision of a total knee prosthesis due to periprosthetic infection with a static versus mobile spacer: Controlled randomized study
summary:
The most common complication after installing a total endoprosthesis as a knee replacement is the so-called periprosthetic infection. The tissue around the total knee arthroplasty is inflamed. The current standard for treating the infection is the temporary removal and reinstallation of the knee prosthesis six weeks later. For treatment and bridging, a cement spacer soaked in antibiotics is used in the six-week interval.
There are two types of spacers that are used in revision arthroplasty on the knee joint, the static fixed and the joint-reforming, mobile spacer. The static spacer keeps the knee in an unchangeable position during the six-week bridging phase, while the mobile spacer allows the knee joint a range of motion of up to 60 ° flexion. In this study, the differences between the two types of spacers are determined and elaborated, especially based on the range of motion.
conditions: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to other internal orthopaedic prosthetic devices, implants and grafts

interventions.name: Patients in this group, whose knee endoprosthesis needs to be temporarily removed due to a periprosthetic infection, receive a static spacer for about 6-10 weeks.
Patients in this group, whose knee endoprosthesis has to be temporarily removed due to a periprosthetic infection, receive a mobile spacer for approx. 6-10 weeks.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Infect-related knee arthroplasty removal with temporary spacer installation
-Age. 18-80 years
-Gender: Male, Female
-uncomplicated intraoperative course (e.g. no massive blood loss, no broken bones)
Exclusion criteria:
-BMI> 35
- known mental illness
- known disease of the cardiovascular system, which lead to restrictions in resilience
- known dementia
- known drug abuse
intraoperative or postoperative complications that restrict function or resilience (e.g. hemodynamically relevant bleeding, circulatory or respiratory complications)
-previous operative infection inspection with spacer implantation
